fair_value.method: Blend: 60% forward P/E ($316 = FY2028 EPS ~$10.35, i.e. FY27 consensus $9.58 +8%, with no memory relief before H1 2028, x 30.5), 25% DCF ($280 = $135B forward FCF growing 8%/yr for 10 years, 3.5% terminal, 8.0% discount rate raised for a 5.18% 10-year, $30B net cash, 14.6B shares), 15% sell-side consensus target cross-check ($328). That gives ~$309, rounded to $312 for buyback-driven share-count shrink.

methods.name: Forward P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028 EPS ~$10.35 (FY26 ~$8.86 from 9M $6.88 + ~$1.98 FQ4; FY27 consensus $9.58, ~8% growth; FY28 +8% on price hikes and buybacks, no cost relief) x 30.5 (below today's ~35.6x on FY27 given a 5.18% 10-year and a hiking Fed; above the 25-30x 5-year average given the product cycle and ~$100B/yr buybacks)

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Forward FCF $135B, 8% growth for years 1-10, 3.5% terminal growth, 8.0% discount rate (5.2% risk-free plus a compressed ERP on a very high-quality balance sheet), +$30B net cash, 14.6B diluted shares. At a 7.5% discount rate it is ~$318, which shows how much the value depends on rates

methods.name: Sell-side consensus cross-check
methods.inputs: Mean analyst target ~$328 (median ~$340, range $215-405); used only as a sanity check on market expectations, not as an anchor

bear.story: Memory at ~$2.00/Gb DRAM (+33%) and +30-40% NAND for 2027 outruns price increases. After the $100 Pro hike and the $1,999 Duo, units disappoint, gross margin guides below 46%, and FY27 EPS is cut to ~$9.1. With the 10-year above 5% and the Fed still hiking, the multiple de-rates to ~27x. Tail adds: a mid-2027 D.C. Circuit ruling that reinstates a ban on Google default-search payments, and a punitive China chip-tariff rate from 2027-06-23. Result ~$245.

base.story: The iPhone 18 Pro/Duo cycle holds up (Pro lead times rose to 21-30 days in the US and Europe), and FY27 EPS lands near $9.6-9.8 as price increases roughly offset memory costs, with gross margin around 46.5-47.5%. Services grows ~11-12% in constant currency. The market rolls forward to FY28 EPS of ~$10.35 at ~33x despite high rates, so the stock is about flat.

bull.story: A genuine super-cycle: Duo and Pro demand stays supply-constrained through 2027, Gemini-based Siri drives an accelerated upgrade cycle, and price increases more than cover memory so margins hold ~47%+. Yields retreat from the 19-year high as inflation cools. FY28 EPS ~$11.2 at ~38x gives ~$425. Probability trimmed from 0.25 because memory relief in 2027 is ruled out and rates are a headwind.

thesis_break_reason: About -27% from $341, just above the 52-week low of $243 and ~26x FY27 consensus EPS of $9.58. With a 5.18% 10-year yield and a hiking Fed, a pure rate-driven de-rating to ~28x on unchanged estimates (~$268) is ordinary volatility, not a broken thesis, so I lowered the level from $255. A sustained close below ~$250 would most likely mean earnings estimates are being cut: gross margin guided well below 46% as $2/Gb DRAM outruns pricing, iPhone 18/Duo unit declines after the price hikes, an appellate ruling that ends the ~$20B Google payment, or a punitive China semiconductor tariff rate in June 2027.

reasoning: Round 2 changes. The supervisor established, and I verified, four things I missed or got wrong in round 1. (1) The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, with 16 of 19 members expecting another hike, and the 10-year closed at 5.18% on 2026-09-25, a 19-year high. A 35.6x forward P/E means a ~2.8% earnings yield against a >5% risk-free rate, so the multiple has more room to fall than rise, and I cut my target multiple from 32x to 30.5x. (2) Memory does not ease in 2027. Apple accepted ~$2.00/Gb DRAM (vs $1.50) and ~+30-40% NAND for 2027, with no relief expected through 2028. My round-1 assumption of relief 'into 2028' was too early, so FY28 EPS drops from ~$10.50 to ~$10.35 and margins depend on price increases. (3) FY26 EPS is ~$8.86 (9M $6.88 + FQ4), so FY27 consensus of $9.58 is only ~8% growth and includes the lapping of one-off tariff refunds. (4) The China chip tariff steps up on 2027-06-23, which I had omitted. I partly disagree with the supervisor on the Google payment: it treats the payment as a tail risk, but DOJ's cross-appeal explicitly asks the D.C. Circuit to ban payments to distributors, and a decision is likely by mid-2027, inside the horizon. I therefore keep slightly more left-tail weight on it. I also accept that the Services slowdown is mostly FX, which is mildly less bearish than my round-1 view. New methods: forward P/E $316, DCF $280 (very sensitive to the discount rate; $318 at 7.5%), consensus-target cross-check $328, blended to a fair value of ~$312 (from $335). The forecast median is above fair value because the rate shock is already in the $341 close and the product cycle has real momentum: Pro lead times rose to 21-30 days in the US and Europe, although China is weaker. The scenario mix (27% at $245, 50% at $340, 23% at $425) has a mean of ~$334. For the ladder I used a lognormal centered at ~$332 with 28% log-volatility (the 25% realized vol plus rate, memory and legal risk), with a slightly heavier left tail. That gives P(>=341) = 0.465, a ~24% chance of being below $273 and ~12% above $460. I did not use option-implied data or anything under valuation/priors/.
